text:
Vera: Quick flag  after the routing rollout the latency dashboard shows p95 < p50 on /v1/complete in eu-west-2 for the 15m window. p95=75ms, p50=170ms.
Hector: That's a red flag for merge/sampling mismatch. Any recent sampler or routing multipliers?
Vera: We enabled a low-cost fallback for throttled clients 18m ago. Sampler logs show fallback events were oversampled (multiplier 8x) compared to primary.
Zoe: If our rollup uses raw sample counts as weights when merging tdigest objects, oversampled fallback will pull merged percentiles toward the fallback distribution. That can invert p95/p50.
Hector: Short-term mitigation: add a console smoke panel showing per-origin p50/p95 and the raw vs effective counts, and display a yellow badge when merged_p95 < merged_p50.
Vera: Agreed. Also add an automated pre-rollout check: run a 10m test window and abort the rollout if merged percentiles invert.
Zoe: Medium-term fix: change aggregator to carry per-origin effective_count (instrumentation multiplier * raw_samples) and perform weight-aware tdigest merges or compute weighted histograms. I'll open the telemetry PR with unit tests simulating sampling skew.
InfraBot: Created ticket INC-2026-120: "fallback-oversample-percentile-inversion". Tasks: console-panel, pre-rollout-smokecheck, telemetry-weighted-merge. Link: https://redwood/internal/inc/INC-2026-120
Hector: +1. Add eng-runtime to the incident so routing rollouts include the smokecheck in their checklist.
Vera: I'll put a minimal repro query into the runbook: ```SELECT sample_origin, count(*) raw_n, percentile(response_ms,0.95) p95, percentile(response_ms,0.5) p50 FROM requests WHERE endpoint='/v1/complete' AND ts>now()-15m GROUP BY sample_origin;``` and instructions to compute weighted merge.
